body:
<!-- pr-reviewer: d2455e145cd2e1f6c9c0ebca511a334591b97e93 -->
Ready for the maintainer to merge, after parent PR #1753. (Final M5 review of the head a first-pass review already cleared.)

Read against current upstream `AGENTS.md` and `assets/machines/AGENTS.md`.

**What looks good**
- Every travel, rpm, kW (except the Mini Mill note below), feed, rapid, pocket count and taper checks out against Haas-published figures: the Haas product pages cited in `docs/decisions/1976-haas-machines.md` (haascnc.com returned 403 to my fetches, so I could not re-read those pages) and Haas's own published "Haas CNC Guide, Issue 18" (haas.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Haas-CNC-Guide-Issue-18.pdf), which states VF-2 762 x 406 x 508 mm, 8,100 rpm, 40-taper, 30 hp (22.4 kW), 20-tool carousel; VF-2SS 12,000 rpm, 30+1 SMTC, 35.6 m/min rapids; DT-1/DM-1 508 x 406 x 394 mm, 10,000 rpm, 30-/40-taper, 20+1 / 18+1, 61.0 m/min rapids, rigid tapping to 5,000 rpm; Mini Mill 406 x 356 x 381 mm, 8,000 rpm, 40-taper, 10 or 20 pockets.
- Feed/rapid conversions are right: 650/1000 ipm = 16510/25400; 1400 ipm = 35560; 1200/2400 ipm = 30480/60960; VF-2SS 833 ipm = 21158.2 rounded DOWN to 21158. The Mini Mill 400 ipm cap is lower than the current standard Mini Mill's published rates, so it is the conservative side.
- Travel bands use the documented `-L..L` program-coordinate rule (`assets/machines/AGENTS.md`, "travel"), the same as the Tormach files; Z `safe_retract` 0.0 states top home. No band is wider than that rule gives.
- No post/CPS file changed, so no overlap with #1821 / #1738 (both edit `haas.cps` and others; neither touches machines or `posting::MACHINES`). #1681 touches `posting.rs` (different function), as the body says.
- Clean-room: original JSON, numbers only, sources cited, no Autodesk/Fusion material. Decision file present, no new crate dependency, no process files touched, no snapshot PNGs.
- Mergeable with current upstream main (clean `git merge-tree`).

**Results (locally, on the PR head, Haas files + parent #1753 included; main not merged beyond a clean merge-tree check)**
- `camcraft-app` tests: haas_machines 3/3, machine 33/33, sinker_burn 15/15, machine_library 11/11, machine_switch 6/6, post_serves_kind 6/6, posting 17/17, rigid_tapping 5/5, post_not_judged 4/4 - all pass.
- `camcraft-ui --lib machine_mode`: 9/9 pass.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- No GitHub Actions workflow was dispatched. The remaining quick-gate suites were not re-run; the plan lists them (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main --dry-run`) and the PR body reports them green.

**Requested before merge**
None blocking.

**Questions / notes (not blocking)**
1. `assets/machines/haas-mini-mill.mch:16` states `"power": 7.5` (kW), taken from #1976. Haas's guide above lists the redesigned Mini Mill at "7.5 hp", which is about 5.6 kW. So 7.5 kW overstates the published figure by a third. `power` is display-only (no limit reads it), so it gates nothing, but please either correct it to 5.6 or record in the decision file why 7.5 kW is kept. The decision file also does not cite a power source for the Mini Mill.
2. DT-1 / DM-1 allow `max_speed` 10,000 rpm with `rigid_tapping: true`, while Haas publishes a 5,000 rpm rigid-tapping ceiling; the PR discloses this and the control, not CamCraft, would refuse. A follow-up issue for a tapping-rpm ceiling would be worthwhile.
3. The DT-1 and Mini Mill are shipped with their optional-spindle (12k/15k/20k) and changer variants out; the standard values are what is stated, which is the safe side.
4. The PR includes parent #1753's commits (sinker template and UI); merge #1753 first, as the body says.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
